concept_card.statement: A narrower slit gives a wider central maximum, and a tilted polaroid between crossed polaroids lets some light through.
concept_card.analogy: Like a vertical gate then a horizontal gate: a slanted gate between lets some through.
steps: First minima: a sin θ = ±λ, so central width ≈ 2λD/a.
Polaroid: I = I0 cos²θ; unpolarised gives I0/2.
Crossed pair plus 45° middle sheet: (I0/2)cos²45°cos²45° = I0/8.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: If I make the slit thinner, the bright spot on the screen gets thinner too.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: For big openings a smaller window really does give a smaller patch of light.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: When the slit is only a few wavelengths wide, light diffracts; the first minima sit at sin θ = λ/a, so a smaller a pushes them outward.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: The central maximum width 2λD/a grows as the slit width a shrinks.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Double Slit, 'cover one slit' mode: narrow the slit and watch the single-slit envelope (width 2λD/a) spread out.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: A polaroid only blocks light, so adding another one can only make things darker.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Every extra filter usually cuts more light, and one polaroid already halves unpolarised light.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: A polaroid also sets the direction of polarisation. Crossed polaroids give 0, but a 45° sheet between them turns the light so (I0/2)cos²45°cos²45° = I0/8 passes.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: A polaroid passes the component along its axis, so a tilted middle polaroid can increase the light through a crossed pair.

contrast_probes.probe: Which of these can make light reach a spot that was dark before: narrowing a slit, or adding a polaroid between two crossed polaroids?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Only the polaroid one — a narrower slit just makes the bright band thinner.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Only the narrower slit — a polaroid can only block light.

contrast_probes.probe: You halve the slit width. Does the first dark band on the screen move closer to the centre or farther away?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Closer, because the whole pattern shrinks with the slit.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Farther, because sin θ = λ/a doubles when a is halved.

contrast_probes.probe: Two crossed polaroids give a dark screen. You slide a third one at 45° between them. Does the screen stay dark or get some light?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: It stays dark, because another polaroid can only block more.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It gets some light, I0/8, because the middle sheet turns the polarisation.

verify_flags: I0/8 assumes ideal polaroids with no extra absorption
